c.tagline: German colonial charm, Tsingtao beer, and Yellow Sea beaches on China's Shandong coast.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and cheap; most drivers speak little English, so show your destination in Chinese. Mobile payment (Alipay/WeChat) is expected, though cash still works.

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police, 120 for ambulance/medical, and 119 for fire. English-speaking operators are limited, so having your location written in Chinese helps.

avoid.reason: Confirm seafood prices in writing before ordering at beachside restaurants without posted menus, and mind pickpockets in beer-festival and beach crowds.

hood_desc: The historic German-colonial core of Shinan around Zhongshan Road, the red-roofed old town, St. Michael's Cathedral, and the century-old Zhanqiao Pier reaching into the bay; best for first-timers who want landmarks, beaches, and old architecture on foot.

A leafy seaside villa district of winding streets named after China's eight great passes, lined with early-20th-century European mansions, the Huashi Villa (Chiang Kai-shek's former retreat), and quiet No. 2 Bathing Beach; suits travelers after scenery, photos, and a slow romantic stroll.

The modern Shinan waterfront and CBD around May Fourth Square, the red 'May Wind' sculpture, the Olympic Sailing Center, and Fushan Bay; a walkable base with the city's top hotels, malls, and skyline promenade.

The green mountain-and-coast district east of the city where Laoshan, China's highest coastal peak, meets the sea, dotted with Taoist temples, tea villages, and the Shilaoren beach resort strip; ideal for hiking, day-trips, and nature over nightlife.

The dense, local northern districts of Shibei and Licang centered on the Taidong pedestrian and night-market street; budget-friendly, packed with street food, mural alleys, and everyday city life away from the tourist coast.

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; avoid tap water and ice made from it.

transit.hours: Metro runs roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; buses generally from around 5:00 AM to 9-10 PM, with limited late-night lines.
transit.note: Qingdao has a growing metro network (Lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 11, and 13) plus an extensive bus system; the coastal old town is best explored on foot, with the metro and taxis linking outer districts and beaches.
transit.pay: Tap the rechargeable Qintong (Qindao Tong) card, or scan a QR code via the Metro Qingdao app, Alipay, or WeChat; single metro fares start around ¥2. Cash is accepted on buses (exact change) but mobile payment dominates.

bus: Long-distance coaches to other Shandong cities

car.idp: Not valid (foreign and international permits are not recognized; a temporary Chinese permit is required)

ferry: Qingdao-Huangdao passenger ferry across Jiaozhou Bay
train: High-speed rail from Qingdao and Qingdaobei stations to Jinan, Beijing, and Shanghai

transit.m: Metro Line 8 toward the city, transfer for downtown Shinan (~60-90 min)
Taxi to downtown Shinan (~50-70 min depending on traffic)
Airport shuttle bus lines to major city hubs (~60 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected anywhere in mainland China; no service charge at local restaurants, though high-end hotels may add one.
